title: Factorial Calculator
description: Calculate factorials iteratively and recursively, handle edge cases, and work with arrays.

steps.title: Factorial with a loop
steps.description: Write a `factorial` function that calculates n! (n factorial) using a `for` loop. Factorial of n is `n * (n-1) * (n-2) * ... * 1`.
hints: Multiply result by each number from 1 to n

codeTemplate.python:
def factorial(n):
  result = 1
  
  return result

print(factorial(5))
print(factorial(3))

verification.failureMessage: factorial(5) should return 120, factorial(3) should return 6.

steps.title: Recursive factorial
steps.description: Write a `factorialRecursive` function that calculates n! using recursion (a function that calls itself).
hints: The function calls itself with a smaller value each time

verification.failureMessage: factorialRecursive(5) should return 120, factorialRecursive(3) should return 6.

steps.title: Handle edge cases
steps.description: Update the factorial function to handle edge cases: 0! = 1 and negative numbers should return an error message.
hints: If n < 0, return an appropriate error message like 'Factorial not defined for negative numbers'
Check for these cases at the start of your function

verification.successMessage: Edge cases handled: 0! = 1 and negative numbers give an error!

steps.title: Factorials of an array
steps.description: Write a function that takes an array of numbers and returns a new array with each number's factorial.
hints: Use .map() in JS/TS or a list comprehension in Python

steps.title: Sum of factorials
steps.description: Write a function that calculates the sum of factorials for all numbers in an array.
hints: Use your factorialArray function and then sum the results
Use .reduce() in JS or sum() in Python
